mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a single month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 50% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.5% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 50% of instances following two consecutive quarters of GDPC1 decline.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a single month signals a robust supply-side response, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO rises > 2% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market with strong job growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 50% of instances when UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increase > 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals weakening consumer demand, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when RSAFS decreases > 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals inflationary pressure amidst tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real returns are eroded.
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over two consecutive months signals a strengthening supply-side response in the housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic activity and consumer confidence improve.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 50% of instances following two consecutive months of HOUST increase.
